newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends touch lower after LME stock hike.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends touch lower after LME stock hike.

text.p: COMEX copper barely ended weaker in a light, choppy session as a moderate LME stock hike countered some of the tightness in December LME, traders said.

"The market was pretty thin but ultimately responded to the hike in LME warehouse stocks," said Bette Raptopoulos of Prudential Securities. "This is a seasonal increase that occurs at the end of the business year."
LME stocks rose 7,225 tonnes to 112,500 tonnes on Friday. LME stocks in the U.S. rose 7,400 tonnes in Long Beach, Baltimore and St Louis.
The hikes in U.S. and Singapore LME stocks were partially countered by falls in Europe.
March COMEX settled 0.40 cent weaker at 99.30 cents per pound, traded 100.20 to 98.50 cents. Spot December went out 0.10 cent lower at 102.50 cents.
The recent hike in U.S. LME stocks was simply metal being transferred from COMEX warehouses to LME, traders said, though some believed this shuffle has now largely drawn to a close.
In the short-term, the market was monitoring next Monday's Third Wednesday pricing on LME to see how the tightness, which has been holding up the market, will resolve itself.
